repo_notes.content: Generate the wiki from the current repository revision and use the implementation as primary evidence. Use README.md, UserGuide.md, Roadmap.md, and docs/guide.html for product status and shipped behavior; use AGENTS.md and the focused guides under agents/ for architecture and contributor contracts. If documentation conflicts with current code, describe the code and call out the discrepancy. Do not cite files absent from the current revision.

JayJay comprises the released native macOS app in shell/mac, reusable Rust crates for jj-aware diff, review state, repository operations, and bindings, and an alpha cross-platform GPUI shell in shell/gpui. SwiftUI reaches Rust through UniFFI; GPUI links the Rust crates directly. Clearly distinguish released SwiftUI behavior, shared core behavior, and GPUI alpha behavior.

Preserve the dependency direction and ownership rules in agents/architecture.md. Document shared domain identity, diff behavior, review reconciliation, and cross-shell stores from their canonical Rust implementations. Use agents/shell-parity.md and the public user guide for user-visible workflows, including exact GPUI gaps and platform-specific SwiftUI features.

Use agents/release.md for releases, agents/storage.md and agents/review-state.md for persisted data, agents/help-book.md for the public site and bundled Help Book, and infra/worker for telemetry and D1 migrations. Keep worker deployment distinct from the Sparkle release flow.

pages.title: JayJay Overview
pages.purpose: Explain the released SwiftUI macOS app, reusable Rust libraries, and alpha GPUI shell; summarize shipped capabilities, requirements, licensing, and current roadmap status from README.md, UserGuide.md, Roadmap.md, docs/guide.html, and current code.

pages.title: System Architecture
pages.purpose: Describe the Rust core, SwiftUI/AppKit shell, direct-linked GPUI shell, UniFFI boundary, business-logic ownership, dependency direction, and async data flow using agents/architecture.md and current source layout.

pages.title: Rust Workspace and Crate Boundaries
pages.purpose: Map every Cargo workspace member and its responsibility, dependency constraints, jj-lib boundary, public surface, and main source modules using Cargo.toml, agents/architecture.md, and the crate manifests and sources.

pages.title: Shared Domain Types and Stores
pages.purpose: Document jayjay-primitives domain and review identity types, jayjay-network helpers, shared repository pins, review storage, platform config paths, atomic writes, corruption handling, and cross-process refresh rules from the canonical Rust implementations and agents/storage.md.

pages.title: Diff Engine and Rendering Model
pages.purpose: Explain jj-diff line and word diffing, syntax highlighting, conflict display, context collapse, wrapping, side-by-side rows, canonical change groups, placeholders, and how both shells consume the shared output; use crates/jj-diff, its README, and renderer code.

pages.title: Review State, Marks, and Notes
pages.purpose: Document jayjay-review marks and notes, content identities, anchor construction, reconciliation, stale and orphaned states, CLI workflows, shell integration, and persistence guarantees using agents/review-state.md and the current Rust and shell implementations.

pages.title: Repository Operations and jj Integration
pages.purpose: Map jayjay-core repository reads and mutations, DAG and revset handling, bookmarks, Git and forge operations, working-copy behavior, conflicts, diff editing, workspaces, undo, stacked pull requests, and the deliberate jj-lib versus jj CLI backend split.

pages.title: Format Projections and Rich Previews
pages.purpose: Explain the blob-to-projection-to-diff-to-render pipeline, supported notebook/table/SARIF/plist projections, raw versus processed modes, cache and review identity, diagnostics, and Markdown/SVG/HTML preview behavior using agents/format-projections.md and both shells.

pages.title: UniFFI Bindings and CLI Dispatch
pages.purpose: Describe jayjay-uniffi as the thin SwiftUI binding layer, generated type conversions and APIs, jayjay-cli launcher behavior, app-owned CLI command forwarding, and GPUI headless review/version dispatch without attributing business logic to the bridge.

pages.title: SwiftUI macOS Shell
pages.purpose: Map shell/mac feature folders, MVVM ownership, SwiftUI and AppKit responsibilities, app lifecycle, menus, onboarding, settings, repository windows, and platform-only integrations using agents/swiftui.md and current sources.

pages.title: SwiftUI Window, State, and Presentation
pages.purpose: Explain RepoViewModel state and action extensions, refresh and supersession rules, multi-window lifecycle, repository list behavior, DAG and detail composition, caching, and the inline/toast/HUD/alert/sheet presentation model.

pages.title: SwiftUI Diff UI and AppKit Renderer
pages.purpose: Document DiffStore and DiffSection, JayJayDiffUI package boundaries, unified and side-by-side rendering, gutter actions, text and media rendering, review notes, selection and diff editing, and rich preview integration.

pages.title: GPUI Cross-Platform Shell
pages.purpose: Map shell/gpui process, CLI, platform, repository, diff, UI, and secondary-window modules; explain supported macOS/Linux behavior, alpha status, direct Rust linkage, native menus, and platform seams using agents/gpui.md and current sources.

pages.title: GPUI State, Tasks, and Rendering
pages.purpose: Explain RepoWindow versus RepoViewModel ownership, background task and generation guards, globals, render caches, filesystem watcher behavior, diff row and note mapping, secondary windows, and headless-safe CLI dispatch.

pages.title: Shell Feature Parity
pages.purpose: Compare user-visible SwiftUI and GPUI workflows from agents/shell-parity.md and current code, preserving shell-native presentation and listing exact current gaps, platform-specific features, and shared contracts without overstating alpha coverage.

pages.title: User Workflows
pages.purpose: Provide a jj-native map of the major user journeys in the current UserGuide.md and docs/guide.html, with links to the implementation pages and explicit SwiftUI/GPUI availability where it differs.

pages.title: Repository Navigation, DAG, and Revsets

pages.title: Diff Review, Notes, and Diff Editing

pages.title: Change Mutations and Conflict Resolution
pages.purpose: Describe new, edit, describe, commit, squash, abandon, rebase, split, duplicate, merge, absorb, back out, operation restore/undo, conflict display, Use Ours/Theirs, and external resolver flows with their backend and shell availability.

pages.title: Bookmarks, Git, and Forge Integrations

pages.title: Workspaces, Stacked Pull Requests, and Inspection Tools

pages.title: Command Palette, Settings, and External Tools
pages.purpose: Document palette actions and raw jj commands, searchable help, settings ownership, editor and terminal integrations, AI commit-message provider fallback, CLI installation, update checks, shortcuts, and shell/platform-specific gaps.

pages.title: Persistence, Caches, Telemetry, and Privacy
pages.purpose: Inventory shared JSON stores, SwiftUI UserDefaults, GPUI TOML config, recent repositories versus shared pins, render caches and disposable files, telemetry identifiers and payload boundaries, path overrides, privacy implications, and deletion behavior using agents/storage.md.

pages.title: Testing and Test Fixtures
pages.purpose: Explain Rust unit/integration test placement, jj-test fixtures, Swift unit tests, XCUITest scenes and accessibility identifiers, GPUI component tests and test globals, fixture isolation, and the smallest appropriate verification layer using agents/testing.md.

pages.title: Build, Development, and CI

pages.title: Release, Signing, Notarization, and Packaging
pages.purpose: Document the complete agents/release.md workflow: synchronized versions, release notes, signed and notarized macOS zip, dSYM archive, Sparkle appcast, GitHub release, Homebrew tap, tags, and asynchronous non-gating GPUI Linux AppImage artifacts.

pages.title: Worker Service and D1 Migrations

pages.title: User Documentation, Website, and Help Book
pages.purpose: Map README.md, UserGuide.md, Roadmap.md, the docs/ GitHub Pages site and machine-readable summary, shared guide assets, bundled macOS Help Book generation and cache behavior, searchable help topics, and update rules from agents/help-book.md.
